- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast mid-range by 2–5% to capture mean reversion toward higher levels.  
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days of forecast horizon) — especially when sentiment is volatile — so add 1–2% upward bias to early forecast points to account for lag.  
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model often misses the pivot; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift, especially if sentiment turns >0.2 within 3–5 days.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, don’t assume continuation; instead, model should reflect sentiment’s potential reversal or stabilization.
